description: Authoritative research dataset of REAL NEC/IFC-required solar PV field placards, labels, stickers, and the service-disconnect directory plaque. Every entry is sourced to a specific code section. Wording, colors, letter heights, and materials reflect ANSI Z535.4 signal-word conventions and NEC 110.21(B) marking rules. Intended to drive the SolarPro permit-planset placard renderer (PV-5 stickers + DISCONNECT PLACARD).
primarySources: HellermannTyton 'PV Labeling NEC 2020 Section 690' white paper
Minnesota DLI 2020 NEC Solar Label Guide
SolarPermitSolutions NEC 690 labeling guides; Mayfield Renewables / Solar Builder NEC-2020 change review; PlansetSigns 705.10 & 706 guides

ansiZ535Reference.note: ANSI Z535.4 defines the signal-word color scheme reused by NEC 110.21(B) safety labels. Signal-word panel colors below are the ANSI standard.

DANGER.meaning: Immediate hazard; will result in death/serious injury

WARNING.meaning: Hazard that could result in death/serious injury

CAUTION.meaning: Hazard that could result in minor/moderate injury

NOTICE.meaning: Information / property-damage message, not a personal-injury hazard

labels.title: Rapid Shutdown Building/Service Placard (with roof diagram)
labels.text:
SOLAR PV SYSTEM IS EQUIPPED WITH RAPID SHUTDOWN
TURN RAPID SHUTDOWN SWITCH TO THE "OFF" POSITION TO SHUT DOWN PV SYSTEM AND REDUCE SHOCK HAZARD IN THE ARRAY.
labels.diagram: Simple line diagram of the building with a roof; array area cross-hatched/shaded to show the PV array boundary; rapid-shutdown initiation-device location indicated.
labels.letterHeightNotes: Title 'SOLAR PV SYSTEM IS EQUIPPED WITH RAPID SHUTDOWN' capitalized, min 3/8 in (9.5 mm). Remaining body text capitalized, min 3/16 in (4.8 mm). NEC 2017/2020 title required WHITE on RED; NEC 2023 dropped the mandated red/reflective color but still requires the diagram + title text.
labels.material: Reflective (2017/2020), UV-resistant weatherproof engraved or laminated; NEC 2023 requires durable/permanent but not specifically reflective.
labels.location: At each service equipment location to which the PV system(s) are connected, or an approved readily visible location (main service disconnect / meter-main).
labels.appliesWhen: rapid shutdown present (all rooftop PV on buildings)
labels.cycleNotes: Wording evolved: 2017 used 'PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM'; 2020 revised to a controlled-conductors description; 2023 standardized on 'SOLAR PV SYSTEM IS EQUIPPED WITH RAPID SHUTDOWN' and relocated the requirement from 690.56(C) into 690.12(D).

labels.title: Rapid Shutdown Array-Boundary / Conductor-Type Label
labels.text: TURN RAPID SHUTDOWN SWITCH TO THE "OFF" POSITION TO SHUT DOWN PV SYSTEM. CONDUCTORS OUTSIDE THE ARRAY BOUNDARY REDUCE TO A SAFE LEVEL.
labels.letterHeightNotes: White capitalized letters min 3/8 in (9.5 mm) on red. Alternate wording for systems that reduce conductors INSIDE the array boundary to a safe level per 690.12(B)(2).
labels.location: On the rapid-shutdown initiation device and/or at the array boundary where conductor-control type must be identified.
labels.appliesWhen: rapid shutdown present; wording selected by controlled-conductor type (inside vs outside array boundary)

labels.title: Rapid Shutdown Initiation Device Label
labels.text: RAPID SHUTDOWN SWITCH FOR SOLAR PV SYSTEM
labels.letterHeightNotes: Capitalized white reflective letters min 3/8 in (9.5 mm) on red. This color scheme is UNCHANGED across NEC 2017/2020/2023.
labels.material: Reflective, weatherproof (mounted on/adjacent to the initiator).
labels.location: On or within 1 m (3 ft) of the rapid-shutdown switch / initiation device.

labels.title: PV System DC Disconnect Marking
labels.letterHeightNotes: Permanent legible marking; must also indicate open(off)/closed(on) position. Wording 'PV SYSTEM DISCONNECT' or equivalent (older editions: 'PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM DISCONNECT').
labels.material: Engraved laminated plastic or durable UV-resistant label; weatherproof if outdoors.
labels.location: On the DC / PV system disconnecting means enclosure.

labels.title: Line/Load Energized-in-Open-Position Warning
labels.text:
WARNING
ELECTRIC SHOCK HAZARD
TERMINALS ON THE LINE AND LOAD SIDES MAY BE ENERGIZED IN THE OPEN POSITION
labels.letterHeightNotes: ANSI Z535 WARNING header. Legible, durable. Some AHJs/kits render this red/white 'DANGER' style; NEC text calls it a warning.
labels.location: On PV system disconnecting means where line and load terminals may be energized in the open position (typical of PV disconnects fed from both directions).
labels.appliesWhen: disconnect line and load terminals may both be energized when open

labels.title: Do Not Touch Terminals / Shock Hazard Warning
labels.text:
WARNING
ELECTRIC SHOCK HAZARD
DO NOT TOUCH TERMINALS
TERMINALS ON BOTH THE LINE AND LOAD SIDES MAY BE ENERGIZED IN THE OPEN POSITION
labels.letterHeightNotes: Commonly furnished as a combined shock-hazard/do-not-touch label on disconnects and combiner boxes.
labels.location: On DC disconnects, combiner boxes, and inverter DC input where energized terminals are accessible.

labels.title: Photovoltaic Power Source (Conduit/Raceway/Combiner Marking)
labels.letterHeightNotes: White capitalized letters on red; ~3/8 in commonly specified. Marks the presence of PV DC circuits so a first responder cutting into a raceway is warned. 2023 permits equivalent wording such as 'SOLAR PV DC CIRCUIT'.
labels.material: UV-resistant weatherproof label (IFC requires reflective/durable outdoors).
labels.location: On exposed raceways, cable trays, cable assemblies, enclosures, combiner/junction box covers, and at intervals not exceeding 10 ft (3 m) and at turns/above-below penetrations.
labels.appliesWhen: PV DC circuits in raceways/enclosures inside a building or exposed

labels.title: DC Photovoltaic Power Source Ratings Label
labels.text:
PHOTOVOLTAIC POWER SOURCE
MAX SYSTEM VOLTAGE:            ____ V DC
MAX CIRCUIT CURRENT (Isc x 1.25): ____ A
RATED MAX POWER-POINT CURRENT: ____ A
RATED MAX POWER-POINT VOLTAGE: ____ V
labels.letterHeightNotes: Machine-printed engraved data label; legible/durable. In NEC 2023 the max-system-voltage data label moved to 690.7(D); 2017/2020 lived in 690.53.
labels.material: Engraved laminated plastic or printed weatherproof label.
labels.location: On the DC PV system disconnecting means or the PV electronic power conversion equipment (inverter/optimizer).

labels.title: AC / Interactive System Point-of-Interconnection Disconnect Rating
labels.text:
PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM AC DISCONNECT
RATED AC OUTPUT CURRENT:  ____ A
NOMINAL OPERATING AC VOLTAGE: ____ V
labels.letterHeightNotes: Interactive-inverter output rating marking. Include a cross-reference to the DC disconnect location.
labels.material: Engraved laminated plastic or durable weatherproof label.
labels.location: On the AC disconnecting means at the point of interconnection.

labels.title: AC Disconnect Identification
labels.letterHeightNotes: Must indicate open/closed position. Utility often requires a visible, lockable, load-side AC disconnect labeled clearly for the lineman.
labels.material: Engraved laminated plastic; weatherproof if outdoors at meter.
labels.location: On the exterior AC disconnect switch (typically near the utility meter).
labels.appliesWhen: utility-interactive; AC disconnect required by AHJ/utility

labels.title: Backfed Breaker "Do Not Relocate" Warning
labels.text:
WARNING
POWER SOURCE OUTPUT CONNECTION
DO NOT RELOCATE THIS OVERCURRENT DEVICE
labels.letterHeightNotes: NEC 2023 wording uses 'POWER SOURCE OUTPUT CONNECTION'; NEC 2017/2020 used 'INVERTER OUTPUT CONNECTION'. Must comply with 110.21(B).
labels.location: On the distribution equipment (main panel/subpanel) adjacent to the back-fed breaker from the PV/power source.
labels.appliesWhen: load-side interconnection via back-fed breaker (busbar/breaker method)

labels.title: Dual Power Source / Inverter-Output Connection Warning
labels.text:
WARNING
DUAL POWER SUPPLY
SOURCES: UTILITY GRID AND PV SOLAR ELECTRIC SYSTEM
labels.letterHeightNotes: Common utility/AHJ-required marking indicating a second power source feeds the equipment. Often paired with the 705.10 directory.
labels.location: On the main service panel / meter-main and any panel fed by more than one source.

labels.title: Multiple Sources of Power / Power-Source Directory Marking
labels.letterHeightNotes: Marking that accompanies the 705.10 directory/plaque (see directoryPlacard). NEC 2023 705.10 requires the plaque to denote the location of each power-source disconnect and be grouped with other on-site source plaques.
labels.material: Permanent engraved plaque; weatherproof if at exterior service.
labels.location: At each service equipment location or an approved readily visible location.

labels.title: Line-Side (Supply-Side) Tap / Service-Connection Warning
labels.text:
WARNING
PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM CONNECTED ON LINE SIDE OF SERVICE DISCONNECT
DO NOT DISCONNECT PV SUPPLY-SIDE CONNECTION WITHOUT DE-ENERGIZING SERVICE
labels.letterHeightNotes: Marks a supply-side / line-side connection ahead of the service disconnect; alerts that the tap remains energized from the utility.
labels.material: Durable engraved or UV-resistant label; weatherproof at meter/service.
labels.location: At the supply-side connection point and on the service equipment/meter-main.

labels.title: "Photovoltaic System Connected" Service Marking
labels.letterHeightNotes: Utility-facing marking on the service so linemen know a generating source is present. Often required by the interconnecting utility in addition to NEC.
labels.material: Durable engraved or UV-resistant weatherproof label.
labels.location: On the utility meter / service disconnect.

labels.title: Energy Storage System Disconnect
labels.letterHeightNotes: Disconnect must indicate open/closed position. For non-1-/2-family dwellings, disconnect marking must also include nominal output voltage, available fault current, arc-flash label, and date of calculation.
labels.material: Engraved laminated plastic or UV-resistant durable label.

labels.title: Energy Storage System Presence Placard / Signage
labels.text:
ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM
ON-SITE ENERGY STORAGE (BATTERY) PRESENT
SEE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE AT SERVICE DISCONNECT
labels.letterHeightNotes: IFC 1207 (and CFC 1207) require durable weather-resistant 'ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM' identification at every external access point, readable from a safe approach distance. A master placard at the main service must indicate presence + location + shutdown procedure.
labels.material: Engraved phenolic, UV-rated vinyl on aluminum, or printed metal placard (fire-marshal accepted).
labels.location: At each external access point to the ESS and at the main service disconnect.

labels.title: Grounding / Bonding Conductor Identification
labels.text: GROUNDING ELECTRODE CONDUCTOR — DO NOT DISCONNECT
labels.letterHeightNotes: Equipment grounding/bonding conductors identified by green (or green/yellow) color per 250.119; GEC connection points labeled where required. Bonding jumpers at array marked.
labels.material: Durable weatherproof label / green tape marker.
labels.location: At grounding electrode conductor terminations, array equipment-ground bonding points, and irreversible ground connections.

labels.title: Inverter / PVRSS Equipment Rating & Listing Label
labels.text:
INVERTER — UTILITY-INTERACTIVE
LISTED PER UL 1741 (SA/SB)
MAX AC OUTPUT: ____ A @ ____ V
RAPID SHUTDOWN: PV RAPID SHUTDOWN EQUIPMENT (PVRSS) — LISTED
labels.letterHeightNotes: Typically factory-applied nameplate; field-verify listing/ratings. Identifies rapid-shutdown method/PVRSS where applicable.
labels.material: Manufacturer nameplate (metal/engraved) + field label as needed.
labels.location: On the inverter / power conversion equipment enclosure.

directoryPlacard.title: Solar/PV System Permanent Directory Plaque at Main Service Disconnect
directoryPlacard.purpose: A single permanent plaque/directory at the main service equipment that (a) marks the presence of PV and any on-site power sources, (b) shows the location of every disconnecting means and PV/ESS equipment via a building directory diagram, and (c) gives first responders the rapid-shutdown / emergency-shutdown steps. Satisfies the grouped power-source directory (705.10), the PV-disconnect-location plaque (690.56(B)), and the rapid-shutdown building placard requirement (690.12(D)/690.56(C)).

sections.heading: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER
sections.contentDescription: ANSI CAUTION header identifying that the building is served by more than one source. Grouped with any other on-site source plaques.
exampleLines: THIS BUILDING IS SERVED BY: UTILITY GRID + SOLAR PV

sections.heading: SYSTEM RATINGS
sections.contentDescription: Key electrical ratings of the PV/ESS output as seen at the point of interconnection.
exampleLines: MAX DC SYSTEM VOLTAGE: ____ V DC
INTERCONNECTION TYPE: LOAD-SIDE BACK-FED BREAKER / SUPPLY-SIDE TAP

sections.heading: LOCATION OF DISCONNECTS & PV EQUIPMENT (DIRECTORY DIAGRAM)
sections.contentDescription: A simple plan/elevation diagram of the building marking the location of each disconnecting means and PV/ESS equipment: main service disconnect, AC PV disconnect, DC/PV system disconnect, inverter(s), rapid-shutdown initiator, and ESS/battery. Each item keyed to the diagram.
exampleLines: 1. MAIN SERVICE DISCONNECT — EXTERIOR, RIGHT OF METER
2. PV AC DISCONNECT — EXTERIOR, LEFT OF METER (LOCKABLE)
3. PV DC / SYSTEM DISCONNECT — AT INVERTER, GARAGE WALL
5. RAPID SHUTDOWN SWITCH — ADJACENT TO PV AC DISCONNECT

sections.heading: RAPID SHUTDOWN
sections.contentDescription: Rapid-shutdown type + roof diagram with array boundary; instruction to operate the initiator. Reproduces the 690.12(D)/690.56(C) placard within the directory.
exampleLines: SOLAR PV SYSTEM IS EQUIPPED WITH RAPID SHUTDOWN
TURN RAPID SHUTDOWN SWITCH TO THE "OFF" POSITION
TYPE: CONDUCTORS OUTSIDE ARRAY BOUNDARY REDUCE TO A SAFE LEVEL (or INSIDE, per system)

sections.heading: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE
sections.contentDescription: Numbered steps a first responder follows to de-energize the system.
exampleLines: 5. ARRAY CONDUCTORS REMAIN ENERGIZED IN DAYLIGHT — TREAT AS LIVE

sections.heading: SYSTEM OWNER / INSTALLER
sections.contentDescription: Installer identification and (NEC 2023 705.10 addition) an off-site emergency/monitoring contact.

directoryPlacard.layoutNotes: Real permanent plaques are laid out as a single durable placard: a CAUTION banner across the top; a labeled building directory DIAGRAM (plan or simple building outline with a roof, array boundary shaded, and numbered callouts to each disconnect) occupying the center-left; a ratings/interconnection block and numbered emergency-shutdown steps on the right; the rapid-shutdown roof diagram + title text in a bottom band. Engraved phenolic or UV-stable printed aluminum, high-contrast, permanently affixed at the service disconnect and readable at eye level. Group with other on-site source directories so all appear together.

notes: CODE CYCLE MATTERS: Always confirm the AHJ's adopted NEC edition (2017 vs 2020 vs 2023) — label wording and section numbers changed. 2023 relocated the rapid-shutdown building placard from 690.56(C) to 690.12(D).

RAPID-SHUTDOWN WORDING CHANGED: 2017 said 'PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM'; 2020 used the controlled-conductor descriptions; 2023 standardized on 'SOLAR PV SYSTEM IS EQUIPPED WITH RAPID SHUTDOWN' and requires a building diagram with the array boundary.

REFLECTIVE / COLOR: NEC 2017 & 2020 mandated the rapid-shutdown building placard be reflective with white on red for the title; NEC 2023 dropped the specific reflective/red color mandate for that placard but the RSD INITIATOR label is still white-on-red reflective across all cycles. Rooftop/outdoor labels must be UV-resistant and weatherproof regardless.

LETTER HEIGHTS DIFFER BY LABEL: RSD title text = min 3/8 in (9.5 mm); RSD body/other body text = min 3/16 in (4.8 mm). 'PHOTOVOLTAIC POWER SOURCE' conduit marking commonly 3/8 in. Data/ratings labels only need to be legible/durable. Do not apply one height to all labels.

BACKFEED BREAKER WORDING: NEC 2017/2020 used 'INVERTER OUTPUT CONNECTION'; NEC 2023 (705.12(B)(3)/705.13) uses 'POWER SOURCE OUTPUT CONNECTION — DO NOT RELOCATE THIS OVERCURRENT DEVICE' to cover all interconnected sources.
MAX DC VOLTAGE LABEL MOVED: In 2017/2020 the DC max-system-voltage data label is 690.53; in 2023 it moved to 690.7(D).

705.10 DIRECTORY (2023): must be grouped with other on-site power-source directories and, new in 2023, include the off-site emergency/monitoring contact; it denotes the location of every power-source disconnect.

ESS DUAL CODE PATH: NEC 706 satisfies the electrical inspector; IFC/CFC 1207 (Chapter 12) satisfies the fire marshal — a battery project generally needs BOTH. ESS ID signage must be at every external access point and readable from a safe approach distance.

ALL 690/705/706 SAFETY LABELS must comply with NEC 110.21(B): permanently affixed, of sufficient durability for the environment, and NOT handwritten. Engraved phenolic or UV-rated printed vinyl/aluminum are the accepted formats.

AHJ / UTILITY VARIATION: Utilities often require an additional visible, lockable, load-side AC disconnect with their own 'PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM CONNECTED' / 'DUAL POWER SUPPLY' wording beyond the NEC minimum. Verify local amendments before finalizing the sticker sheet.

SIGNAL WORDS follow ANSI Z535.4: DANGER (white on red), WARNING (black on orange), CAUTION (black on yellow), NOTICE (white on blue). Some off-the-shelf solar kits render NEC 'WARNING' items in red/white; NEC text calls them warnings — match the adopted standard and AHJ preference.
